cases.purpose: A small spec is drafted grounded and revised completely, one input per variant: a tier S bug with a reproduction first, and a round 2 that must answer two reviewers.

variants.purpose: A tier S bug yields a short, grounded spec whose AC-1 is a failing reproduction, with no team run and no invented paths.

inline.title: Task list sorts by due date as text, so 10 Nov comes before 2 Nov
inline.body: On the task list, click the Due column header. The rows sort as strings instead of dates. Expected: ascending by date. Only the list view is affected; the API returns ISO dates.

tierReasons.evidence: The sort comparator lives in one UI module.

security.reason: No auth or input parsing change.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
status == "ready-for-review" && tier.confirmed == "S" && team is empty
line 3 of spec.md == "Tier: S - Builder: Sol 6.2 - Code reviewer: Opus 5.5"
spec.md has the level 2 headings Problem, Non-goals, Acceptance criteria, Design choices, Reused files, Implementation plan, Risks, Open questions, once each, in that order
every '### AC-n' block has Tag, Fixture, Action, and Expected lines, ids are AC-1..AC-k without gaps, and the ids and tags equal spec-lead.json acceptanceCriteria
AC-1 has Tag: test
every backticked path under Reused files exists in the pilot repository at baseSha
none of team-brief.md, architecture.md, infra.md, frontend.md, threat-model.md exists in outDir
spec.md contains no U+2013 or U+2014 character
Is AC-1 a reproduction of the reported bug whose Expected line states both the correct order and how it fails on the unfixed code?
Is every Expected line something a test or a page capture could observe, with no criterion such as 'sorting works correctly'?
Do the non-goals and plan keep the change inside the list's sort logic, without API, storage, or new-feature work?

variants.pilot: The pilot has the planted bug of triage-01: the task list sorts the Due column as text, with the comparator in one UI module that has an existing test file.

variants.purpose: Round 2. Two verdicts sent the spec back: the spec reviewer's (AC-3 is not observable) and the security auditor's (AC-4 tests only one of the two privileged fields the threat model names). A lead that answers one reviewer and ignores the other fails, as does one that edits the threat model itself.
answerKey: Spec reviewer round 1 finding 1: AC-3's Expected line is not observable. The fix is to state the status code, the absence of task data, and the unchanged task.
Security auditor round 1 finding 1: T-3 names ownerId and id, and AC-4 sends only ownerId. The fix is a criterion, or an extended AC-4, that also sends id and expects refusal.
Neither finding needs the threat model to change, and the lead may not write threat-model.md in any case.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
round == 2 && status == "ready-for-review" && tier.confirmed == "M" && riskFlags.security.value == true
changes has an entry with source "spec-reviewer", round 1, n 1, and an entry with source "security-auditor", round 1, n 1
acceptanceCriteria still lists AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, AC-4 with tag test, any new criterion has a higher id, and retiredCriteria is empty
the AC-3 block of spec.md has an Expected line containing "404"

team has one inherited threat-modeler entry matching previous.decisions in file, originalRound, authorSession and sha256; the runner archives the identical prior bytes and observes no child start or write for that file
outDir holds spec.md and spec-lead.json and no decision file; threat-model.md was not written by the lead's session
line 3 of spec.md == "Tier: M - Builder: Sonnet 5.5 - Code reviewer: Sol 6.2"
Does a criterion now send the task's id (not only ownerId) in an update body and expect the request to be refused with nothing written?
Are AC-1, AC-2, the non-goals, and the design choices unchanged in substance from the round 1 spec?

cases.purpose: Triage under-tiered a schema change. Start the S lead with the team disabled and exercise the fresh team-enabled dispatch after its confirmed promotion to L.
cases.pilot: The pilot of triage-02: tasks are persisted with no priority column, and the UI and API are separate modules. The pilot has a user interface and a database.

inline.title: Quick one: let tasks have a priority
inline.body: Tiny change. Add a priority (low, normal, high) to tasks, show it as a badge in the list, and let me filter by it. Should be a five minute job, just one field.

tierReasons.evidence: The issue requests a badge in the existing task list.

migration.reason: The issue does not name a stored field.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json

the initial team-disabled attempt reports BLOCKED: team required for L with all four members, starts no child and supplies no accepted output; a fresh attempt on a proven team harness authors the spec
tier.provisional == "S" && tier.confirmed == "L" && riskFlags.migration.value == true
line 3 of spec.md == "Tier: L - Builder: Opus 5.5 - Code reviewer: GPT-6.2-Astra"
team has exactly the entries architect, infra, frontend, and threat-modeler, each with status ran, and team-brief.md, architecture.md, infra.md, frontend.md, and threat-model.md exist in outDir
in the harness's record of the run, the architect subagent finished before the infra or frontend subagent started, and both finished before the threat-modeler subagent started
in the harness's record of the run, each decision file was written by its own subagent's session, not by the lead's and not by another member's
each decision file's Task line equals the run brief's taskId and its Author line equals its member's name
every subagent the run started is one of architect, infra, frontend, threat-modeler, and none of those started a subagent
each decision file present has the level 2 headings Decision, Options considered, Rationale, Curated entries used, Catalog gaps, Assumptions

every line under Curated entries used in each decision file names a catalog, and its id is an entries id of that catalog's catalog.json (the threat modeler cites the infra and architecture catalogs, having none of its own)
Does the spec include a criterion or plan step that covers existing task rows getting a priority value when the column is added?
Do the spec's Design choices summarize and point to each decision file rather than contradict or ignore it?

cases.purpose: A conflict that changes acceptance criteria goes to the owner. The lead must not pick a side in the criteria.
cases.pilot: The pilot has an audit export and a committed docs/decisions/retention.md requiring seven years of individually attributable export history.

inline.title: Erase a departed member from export history
inline.body: When I remove a member, every historical audit export must permanently lose the ability to identify that person, including exports regenerated for past years.

tierReasons.evidence: Member removal changes the historical audit export.

security.reason: Changes the handling of identifying data in audit history.

expect.check: spec-lead.json validates against spec-lead/spec-lead.schema.json
status == "needs-owner"
escalations contains an item with kind == "ac-conflict" and at least 2 options
conflicts contains an item with changesAcceptanceCriteria == true whose between includes a path under docs/decisions/
the Open questions section of spec.md contains a line starting with "- [blocking]"
at least one acceptanceCriteria item has pendingEscalation == true
Does the spec avoid committing, in its acceptance criteria, to either removing all attribution from past exports or retaining it for seven years?
Does each escalation option say what it would do to the acceptance criteria, so the owner can answer in one line?
